reference: There is no GNU or POSIX auth command corresponding to this Bash loadable. Runnable expectations use Bash builtin metadata and the published auth help contract in the documented source for auth.c. They do not claim GNU command parity. Device, credential, and authorization operations are deferred for a disposable VM or a reviewed mock.
coverage: Bash reports auth and help as builtins through type -t.
Bash help metadata contains the documented auth API surface.
auth --help, auth -h, and auth help agree and include documented API entries.
Deferred operation plans identify device ABI, PTY secret handling, synthetic credential verification, and isolated authority/child behavior.
Pure in-memory path glob match, no-match and argument validation, without credentials or authority activity.
exclusions: No device, credential, installed policy, user identity or authority operation executes; pure path-string evaluation is covered separately.
No GNU auth CLI exists, so no synthetic parity oracle is claimed.
Policy parsing/listing, per-user authentication counters, kernel tokens, audit records and privileged child transitions remain unverified.

cases.purpose: Confirm through Bash's type builtin that the selected auth loadable is registered as a builtin and that help is available as a shell builtin.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t auth) == builtin ]]
[[ $(type -t help) == builtin ]]
printf 'auth=builtin; help=builtin\n'

cases.purpose: Check the Bash help database exposes the documented device, sealed-secret, login-verification, and per-user API entries from auth_doc.
cases.script:
doc=$(help auth)
[[ $doc == *'Talk to /dev/bashos-auth - kernel-mediated authority tokens.'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'auth open FDVAR'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'auth read-secret FD [-p PROMPT] HANDLEVAR'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'auth verify-login FD HANDLE USER PHC TOKENVAR'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'peruser tracks per-user failed-attempt caps independent of the'* ]]
printf 'Bash help contains documented auth API entries\n'
cases.stdout: Bash help contains documented auth API entries

cases.purpose: Verify the three documented help spellings return the same help text and that it contains stable API text from auth_doc.
cases.script:
long=$(auth --help)
short=$(auth -h)
named=$(auth help)
[[ $long == "$short" ]]
[[ $short == "$named" ]]
[[ $long == *'auth policy-parse FILE  validate and normalize sudoers subset'* ]]
[[ $long == *'auth privcmd-token FD HANDLE'* ]]
[[ $long == *'The fd from `open` owns all secret slots'* ]]
printf 'auth help aliases agree with the documented API\n'
cases.stdout: auth help aliases agree with the documented API

cases.purpose: Future operation coverage for version probing, opening the authority descriptor, per-descriptor counters, secret clearing, close-on-exec behavior, and cleanup.
cases.reason: Everything except the absent-device diagnostic needs the authority device. guest /dev/bashos-auth v2 UAPI implementation (kernel module or a root-owned CUSE character-device mock implementing loadables/common/_bashos_auth_uapi.h: VERSION, PRIVCMD_AUTHZ, EXEC_VERIFY, EXEC_HANDOFF, token mint/consume, secret slots, policy info). The Debian guest kernel has no such device and the repository holds only the UAPI header, so open() fails with ENOENT and no unprivileged fixture can observe any ioctl behaviour.

cases.purpose: Evaluate literal private path strings with simple star, question and bracket globs; no policy is installed and no path is opened.
cases.script:
auth policy-fnmatch 'fixture/*' fixture/item
auth policy-fnmatch 'fixture/it?m' fixture/item
auth policy-fnmatch 'fixture/[ab]' fixture/a

cases.purpose: A nonmatching private path string prints match=0 and returns 1 without authorization activity.
Missing pure glob arguments are rejected before any device or policy access.
